PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single responsibility aids diagnosis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: look for single Act operation and one Arrange-Act-Assert block. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations (>1 => non-compliant). 2) Check test name for multiple operations. 3) If single method call and assertion group => compliant. VERDICT: The method performs a single act (fila0.desenfileira()) and one try/catch assertion block to validate the exception. No other operations are present. Therefore compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of @Before/@After or only local variables. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for @Before/@After (none visible). 2) Check for shared mutable state (none in method). 3) If only local variables are used => compliant. VERDICT: The test uses only local variables and does not modify static/instance state in the visible snippet; no names implying ordering. Marked compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide tests for happy and error paths. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: For each method under test there should be at least two tests: a happy path and an error path; look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows. DECISION RULES: 1) Count test methods: class shows only one test method; 2) If all tests only exercise error or only happy path => non-compliant. VERDICT: The class (visible snippet) contains only this single test which exercises an exceptional path (desenfileira on empty queue). There is no visible happy-path test for the same method, so the practice is non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundary conditions (empty, zero, etc.). RATIONALE: Many bugs occur at boundaries. EVALUATION CRITERIA: look for empty/zero/negative/max inputs. DECISION RULES: 1) If test data includes empty/zero values, lean compliant. VERDICT: The test explicitly operates on an empty queue and verifies behavior (exception) for that boundary. This matches boundary-value testing for an empty structure, therefore compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and avoid duplication. RATIONALE: Improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of helper methods, constants, or very short tests without repetition. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for helper methods (none). 2) If tests are very short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code => compliant. VERDICT: The test is short and self-contained; no duplication visible in this single-method snippet. Marked compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Low complexity reduces test bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: test methods <20 lines, no loops/conditionals. DECISION RULES: 1) If method <15 lines and linear flow => compliant. VERDICT: The method is small (<20 lines), contains no loops or complex branching beyond a try/catch used to assert exception, and follows a simple Arrange-Act-Assert pattern. Compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: count assertions; if only one (especially assertNotNull/assertTrue) => non-compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) If only 1 assertion is present (or only fail/verifyException) => non-compliant. VERDICT: The test relies on fail() and verifyException to check that an exception was thrown; there is effectively a single behavioral check (exception thrown). There are no additional assertions validating message, state, or properties. Marked non-compliant.
